_comment: A leaderboard export in the `leaderboard@1` shape, produced by THIS
project's own bench harness rather than fetched from a third party.
Every number here was measured, not assumed. Each is one run of
corpus:battery-core-v1 (11 tasks extracted from a real repository at
commit ec7f0bf, each task being a documented function whose body was
removed) scored solely by the repository's own pytest suite. No model,
including the one under test, had any say in whether its output passed.
The harness was calibrated immediately before every run: the oracle
adapter, which restores the original implementation, must score 11/11,
and the stub adapter, which leaves the body unimplemented, must score
0/11. A run that fails either check measures nothing and is discarded.
These are release-level results and carry no worker_id: the measured
configuration was the bench chat adapter, not any rostered worker's
harness. They inform every worker on the release as a prior, capped, and
are outranked by your own lived outcomes the moment you have any.
Scores are the most recent run per model, all taken after the extraction
defect of 2026-08-10 was fixed. Earlier runs measured whether a model
avoided nested helper functions and are deliberately not published.
